function: MIMO symbol detection (DeepSIC equalizer) and soft channel decoding (weighted belief propagation) with calibrated Bayesian soft outputs in an uplink receiver chain (p. 2).
system: Uplink MIMO, K = N = 4 single-antenna users and base-station antennas; no RIS; indoor hall 5 GHz in the COST 2100 case (p. 2, p. 9).
method: Deep-unfolded DeepSIC and WBP modules trained by supervised cross-entropy on pilots with modular Bayesian learning (MC dropout, ensembling); DeepSIC online per block, WBP offline (p. 6-8).
data_channel: Synthetic static linear (exp(-|n-k|)) and tanh non-linear channels; simulated time-varying COST 2100 indoor hall 5 GHz; 128 or 384 pilots per block; polar (128,64) code (p. 9-10).
test_conditions: DeepSIC trained online on each block's pilots, tested on that block's information symbols over an SNR sweep, 10 blocks; WBP trained offline; no unseen scenario (p. 8-10).
baselines: Learned only: frequentist DeepSIC/WBP (F), conventional Bayesian (B), black-box four-layer FC DNN detector; no classical receiver compared (p. 7-8).
metrics: Symbol error rate, bit error rate, expected calibration error versus SNR (p. 9-11).
complexity: none quantified; only the qualitative statement that inference cost grows by the ensemble factor (p. 7).
q2_support: p. 8: "At each block, training is done with 384 pilots" (each block is retrained on its own pilots and tested on its own information symbols; no unseen scenario, configuration or dataset is reported).
q3_support: p. 7: "using as benchmarks frequentist learning and standard, non-modular, Bayesian learning" (all benchmarks and all figure legends are learned: DNN Detector, F, B, MB; no non-learned receiver is compared).
q4_support: p. 7: "the inference complexity increases by the ensemble factor" (qualitative only; no order of complexity, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported).
q5_support: p. 9: "source code used in our experiments is available at https://github.com/tomerraviv95/bayesian-learning-in-receivers-for-decoding"
notes: Read all 13 pages and the figure pages 8-12 as images to check the legends. Included: research article, learned (deep-unfolded) receivers, physical layer, quantitative simulation results, BS with N = 4 antennas. Area 1: the DeepSIC equalizer is MIMO detection; the WBP decoder is channel decoding, which is not one of the seven areas and does not change the area. q1 is met only through the COST 2100 experiments (Fig. 5 and Fig. 10, p. 9-12); the other experiments (Fig. 3, 4, 6) use custom synthetic channels. q3 is 0 because no non-learned detector or decoder is compared: p. 7 says the comparison with state-of-the-art receivers was studied in earlier work [27], [37], and the legends of Figs. 3-10 show only learned schemes (the black-box FC DNN detector and frequentist DeepSIC are learned baselines, but the classical side is missing). q4 is borderline: p. 7 says the inference complexity grows by the ensemble factor (J = 5 for DeepSIC, J = 3 for WBP, p. 8), which I read as qualitative because no order, operations, parameters or runtime are given; the reviewer may overturn. PDF is arXiv v4 (19 Oct 2024) of 'Uncertainty-Aware and Reliable Neural MIMO Receivers via Modular Bayesian Deep Learning'; the DOI-title match could not be checked with the allowed files.
